- The release workflow checks that the packaged updater can open its window.

## How to use it

When Ironmon Tracker offers an update, click **Update**. The tracker fetches the signed Windows x64 updater and opens the review for your installation and selected release. Use Ironmon Setup for a fresh install or a manual update.

If your tracker previously accepted a test updater, it may reject the replacement build as a version reset. Setup remains available for manual updates.

# Ironmon 0.10.2

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Ironmon 0.10.2 is a mutable test prerelease.** This experimental build may
> contain regressions. Downloads may change without a version bump.

## Mutable test release

Use this experimental build at your own risk. Gameplay, tracker features, and
updates may have regressions. The files for v0.10.2 may be replaced during
testing. Keep a separate test installation or back up your game and saves
before upgrading. Finish any active Ironmon run before replacing the game.

If this release is refreshed, download it again. To install a replacement build
with the same version, rerun the latest Setup and explicitly select **0.10.2
(Test release)** under **Advanced: Ironmon version**, or reinstall the complete
matching ZIP. The tracker does not automatically replace a build with the same
version. Setup defaults to stable. In the tracker, **Include test releases**
opts in to newer test versions.

### One-time Setup update

From 0.10.1 or earlier, run the latest signed Setup and point it at your
existing game folder. Select **0.10.2 (Test release)** in the advanced version
options. After this migration, use **Update** in the tracker again.

## What's new

- Updates the base game to **Pokémon Infinite Fusion 2: Hoenn 1.3.2** (engine
  6.9.1). Setup and the combined updater install the matching game revision.
- Updates Ironmon's battle collection, save loading, and encounter handling for
  Hoenn 1.3.2. The game enables 576 base species for fusion.
- Restores older Hoenn saves that have their original generation profile.
  Active attempts keep their seeded evolutions. New attempts use the current
  evolution catalog.
- Moves Ironmon Tracker, Setup, and the updater to **.NET 11**.
- Fixes a .NET 11 packaging crash that could close Setup or the updater before
  its window opened. Download Setup again if you tried an earlier v0.10.2 build.
- Reduces pauses during cold fusion pairing and archived fusion-name loading
  while preserving seeded fusion results.
- Shortens the reset after an opening loss and reveals the starter map directly
  after the battle, including on saves using older starter rules. The Archive
  summary opens without starting lookup calculations until you select the run
  or a lookup tab.
- Shows the installed Infinite Fusion version in tracker settings when the
  signed version record matches the installed game revision.
- Opens a separately signed updater from the tracker. It handles installation
  review and game file preparation, and can receive fixes independently of the
  game and tracker. The update archive uses the signed game file bytes on Windows.
- Renders headings, lists, links, and important notices in the tracker's
  **What has changed** section.

## Windows runtime

If you use **Runtime required**, install the **Windows x64 .NET 11 Runtime**
before updating. **Runtime included** supplies the runtime with the update.

https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/11.0#runtime-11.0.0

Both tracker packages require an x64 CPU that meets the .NET 11 hardware
baseline.

# Ironmon 0.10.1

Ironmon 0.10.1 improves speed-up, loading and calculation responsiveness while
preserving existing runs and archives.

- **Smoother speed-up.** Gameplay pacing is separated from screen updates, with
  a presentation target of up to 120 updates per second. Music keeps its normal
  speed and pitch. Separate battle and overworld settings, Toggle and Hold modes
  remain available.
- **More predictable controls.** Held menu inputs repeat at their normal
  real-time cadence while walking stays accelerated. Rapid speed-stage changes
  preserve each selection and smooth the transition between speeds.
  Move-learning protection remains in place.
- **Clearer transitions.** Encounter effects, battle introductions and fades run
  at no more than 3× speed before returning to the selected gameplay speed.
- **Preparation before play.** Loading an Ironmon save finishes game preparation before
  returning control to the map. The game shows a simple waiting message, while
  the tracker temporarily fills its window with an animated preparation view
  and the current step. The normal tracker page returns without shifting.
- **Responsive calculations.** Automatic calculations use small background
  slices during play. Opening an archived run or requesting visible lookup data
  gives that calculation foreground priority and continues its existing work.
  Preparing uncached lookup data also causes fewer long pauses.
- **Adjusted fusion stats for new runs.** Seeded stat contributions now use
  85/15, 75/25 and two-thirds/one-third weights. The game and tracker use the same
  formula. Existing runs and archives keep their recorded formulas and stats;
  normal Pokémon stat generation is unchanged.
- **Sky Drop recovery.** Carried Pokémon are released correctly when damage is
  prevented or the move is interrupted, including the Wonder Guard case.
- **Volt Switch and U-turn visibility.** Both moves still deal damage when no
  eligible replacement exists, and the user remains visible afterward. Normal
  switching and fainting behavior is preserved.
- **More reliable Windows updates.** The updater handles temporary file locks
  more reliably when preparing and cleaning its download cache.

# Ironmon 0.10.0

Ironmon 0.10.0 is a substantial update from 0.8.15. It changes fusion generation
and the opening rival sequence, adds independent starter rules, brings the
wardrobe into the tracker, and introduces persistent gameplay collection,
achievements, richer Pokémon history, configurable speed cycles, and more
accurate world lookup.

- Setup can replace an earlier 0.10.0 test build without treating its original
  program files as local edits. Use the corrected Setup once when upgrading
  from a build that predates this fix.
- Losing the opening rival battle now qualifies for its achievement using the
  game's actual encounter identity. The first main-rival victory milestone
  requires five wins across runs; later rival milestones keep their thresholds.
  Existing unlocks remain earned, and main-rival and Wally victories stay separate.

## Fusion generation and concealed choices

- **New fusion stat inheritance for new runs.** Body- and head-dominant stat
  groups use seeded 90/10, 80/20, and two-thirds/one-third contributions instead
  of the same fixed weighting for every stat. Fusion strength calculations in
  the tracker and game use the same versioned formula.
- **More resilient reverse-fusion pairing.** The new generator can retry the
  complete pairing with progressively wider BST tolerances when a tight pairing
  fails. Shared components remain forbidden; strength tolerance increases in
  five-BST steps, bounded by the pool's full strength range.
- **Useful concealed fusion clues.** Move selection shows a stat-spread
  description and one deterministic, current calculated stat. The other stat
  values remain concealed.
- **Automatic nature inheritance.** A fusion inherits one material's nature
  through a seeded choice. The old nature-selection prompt is removed. Native
  move selection and generated ability assignment are retained.
- Existing runs retain their recorded generation-profile algorithms. The new
  formula and pairing rules do not silently regenerate old runs or archives.

## Independent starter rules and the rival's story

- **Starter Pokémon now have their own run-setting policy:** normal Pokémon,
  custom fusions, or mixed offers, independently of wild and trainer policies.
  The selected policy is preserved in presets, run recipes, and shared seed data.
- The rival takes the actual starter from the original counter slot, preserving
  the slot order even when randomized types no longer form a type triangle.
- After the first rival victory, the trainer policy determines whether the
  rival keeps its partner, swaps to the remaining offer, unfuses, or fuses the
  two normal offers. The resulting partner persists through the later story.
- The lab sequence now handles those branches with Birch's assistance, native
  fusion animation, and movement around the player, furniture, and doorway.
  Rival fusion does not replace the player's party or register its Pokémon as
  the player's catches.
- Rival fusion assignments and additional evolution work are prepared through
  the tracker. Large result imports are processed in smaller game updates to
  reduce long pauses after the opening battle.
- A loss or draw in the Route 101 rescue or first rival battle always ends the
  attempt and queues a safe reset, including when automatic loss reset is off.
  The failed attempt is recorded and Archive opens without delaying reset for
  completed-run lookup calculations.
- Earlier configuration-version-1 runs and seed data remain supported, retaining
  their original wild-controlled starter policy and rival plan.

## Progression, rewards, and battle safeguards

- Limited-party trainer battles now enter the current healthy Ironmon runner
  automatically, without asking the player to select a team. This includes
  Gym Leaders, regional adventurers, and move tutors. Type restrictions still
  apply, and multi-Pokémon quest hand-ins retain their normal selection rules.
- **The first Alpha endpoint is recorded as a win.** Winning Wattson's normal
  Hoenn Gym battle completes the attempt, updates win statistics and achievement
  evidence, and saves the completed state after battle and event cleanup.
  Duplicate battle reports cannot award the win again.
- **A Pokémon Center recovery gift is available once per attempt.** Its item is
  selected deterministically from the run's seed, so repeating the interaction
  does not reroll or repeatedly award the gift.
- Direct scripted trainer rematches now obey the same challenge restriction as
  menu rematches, including rival and Tiana rematch paths. One-time story battles
  remain available.
- Move-forgetting selection waits for Confirm/Cancel to be released before
  accepting a new input. Move-learning protection also prevents accelerated
  frames from carrying a held action straight into an unintended choice.

## Tracker wardrobe and cosmetic rewards

- **Wardrobe editing now happens in a game-opened tracker dialog.** Use the
  game's Change outfit command or bedroom wardrobe. Gameplay and the attempt
  timer pause while editing; Apply or Cancel returns to the game.
- Fresh characters with an empty second accessory slot can open the wardrobe
  without the tracker disconnecting and reconnecting repeatedly.
- Browse searchable outfits, hairstyles, and two accessory layers, with filters
  for all, owned, or unowned pieces. Locked pieces can be previewed before purchase.
- Native previews cover the detailed portrait, front/back/side views, and bicycle.
  Skin tone, installed hair colors, and hair/clothes/accessory/bicycle dyes are
  editable, including precise hue values.
- **Named outfit profiles** can be saved, applied, renamed, replaced, and deleted.
  Each save slot keeps its confirmed appearance through loading and resets.
- Purchases are permanent even if an equipped preview is cancelled. Reconnection
  restores the current draft and ownership; physical Back can leave the wardrobe
  if the tracker disconnects.
- **Permanent unlock prices are five times their previous values.** Existing
  point balances and owned pieces are retained without rescaling or extra charges.
  Colors and dye remain free, and the profile-wide additional free selection is
  retained until confirmed.
- **Each newly earned achievement grants 100 wardrobe points.** Rewards are
  queued durably and credited once, including after a disconnect or lost
  acknowledgement. Achievement pop-ups do not need to be enabled. Achievements
  already earned before this reward system was introduced are not paid retroactively.

## Persistent achievements and artwork

- Fixed achievement tracking silently remaining inactive in clean Setup
  installations. Collector startup errors are now visible in protocol diagnostics.
- A new **Achievements** page provides earned names, requirements, unlock dates,
  collection progress, search, and sorting. Progress and earned unlocks persist
  across attempts, resets, and save slots.
- Locked names, conditions, and artwork stay concealed. Recorded evidence can
  contribute to later stages as their prerequisites become active.
- Earned achievements have dedicated icons. Clicking supported earned icons
  opens their larger detail artwork. Artwork is shipped in protected embedded
  packs rather than loose image folders.
- Compact in-game notifications show the earned icon and title, queue unlocks
  individually, and follow the game window's position and display size.
  They use a native Windows overlay without WPF, retaining sharp 50-, 75-, and
  100-pixel artwork, transparency, click-through behavior, and game-controlled timing.
- Compatible achievement-definition and artwork updates retain earned identities
  and original unlock dates. Collection begins when the new recorder is used;
  importing a seed does not recreate older, unrecorded gameplay.

## Gameplay collection and history maintenance

- The tracker now records gameplay evidence in a persistent SQLite collection,
  covering Pokémon ownership and history, battle activity, resources, items,
  progression, and cosmetic events. Journaled delivery and duplicate protection
  support recovery across reconnects and interrupted sessions.
- **Settings > Maintenance** reviews and exports unrelated history with the game
  closed. A closed game also permits maintenance after a connection-error state.
- Review rehearses the real export, removal, and compaction on an owned temporary
  database copy. The displayed estimate is conservative **net disk space freed**,
  including the archive remaining on the same drive, rather than expanded JSON
  record size. The live database, WAL, and recipes remain unchanged during review.
- Export creates a compressed, encrypted `.irmhistory` archive and verifies it
  before removing eligible source records. Protection is automatic: the player
  does not choose or receive a password.
- Achievement evidence, earned unlocks, shared identities, live checkpoints, and
  Pokémon configuration chains remain in the active profile. Completion reports
  measured disk savings, including additional space used when an export grows.
- Import restores an archive to its originating profile, merges it with newer
  evidence, and prevents duplicate counting. Keep exported files: future
  achievements may need detached history, and deleting the archive loses it.
- Reconnecting the game discards a stale maintenance review and requires a fresh
  measurement before changing history.

## Pokémon history, IVs, and archive inspection

- **Owned-Pokémon IV inspection** adds recorded individual values to Pokémon
  lookup, including effective values and Hyper Training where that information
  is available. When several owned individuals share a species, their records
  can be inspected separately.
- **Archive Pokémon history** retains the last Pokémon and earlier recorded
  starter, pivot, fusion, and evolution stages, with their highest recorded
  levels. Selecting a stage opens its archived species information.
- Saved checkpoint boundaries trim discarded continuations after a reload,
  keeping the retained Pokémon timeline aligned with the saved attempt.
- Archived sprites are reused offline. Missing history sprites can be requested
  from the connected game in bounded batches and cached for later viewing.
- Losing opening-rival runs retain the context needed for later trainer-team
  inspection. Generating that preview is deferred until explicitly requested.

## Trainer, encounter, and obtainability lookup

- Trainer catalog generation now follows additional scripted story-battle paths
  and links multiple event identities to the correct trainer entry.
- Rival, Wally, and other supported story teams can use their actual persistent
  story Pokémon when preparing trainer lookup, rather than treating every member
  as a fresh generic trainer randomization.
- Trainer battle completion and item completion better follow their actual event
  identities, completion switches, and self-switches.
- Encounter and obtainability calculations filter tables by the encounter methods
  the map can actually trigger, including land, cave, water, fishing, weather, and
  time variants. Unused encounter data no longer creates false available sources.
- Early manual lookup preparation and authorized evolution inspection can prepare
  required fusion assignments before normal background lookup has started.
- Additional cooperative checkpoints reduce long game-thread work during fusion
  closure, encounter expansion, and completed-run lookup preparation. Existing
  hidden-information restrictions remain in force.

## Battle quick items, speed, and settings

- **An in-game battle item selector** browses items and categories, remembers the
  selected item in each category between battles, and uses normal battle
  usability and targeting checks. Its controls are configurable in the tracker.
- Five new battle bindings cover previous/next item, previous/next category, and
  use. Keyboard defaults use Ctrl+Shift with arrows and C; mapped controllers use
  both triggers with the D-pad and confirm button.
- **Settings > Speed** edits independent overworld and battle Toggle cycles,
  using multipliers from 2× to 10×, custom order, repeated values, grouped stages,
  and links between contexts. Groups remember their selected member and define
  their first-entry speed. Normal speed remains first.
- The speed editor includes Undo, Redo, and explicit Save changes. Hold mode
  retains the game's separate overworld/battle sliders. A new optional overworld
  indicator shows the active multiplier and cycle position; the Repel display
  uses the shared overlay styling.
- Settings now have **General, Controls, Features, Speed, and Maintenance** pages.
  Features groups achievement pop-ups, Repel/speed indicators, item quick select,
  quick Run, Favorite Clause, BST enforcement, starter autoselection, automatic
  loss reset, and minimized startup.
- Turning assistance off preserves its saved favorites, values, item selections,
  and bindings. Disabled quick-item/Run bindings remain visible but cannot be
  edited until their feature is enabled again.
- A blank or zero starter BST ceiling means unlimited. Favorite Clause and BST
  enforcement can be switched independently of their saved settings. Saved-state
  feedback no longer shifts the Settings header as it appears.

## Installation, documentation, and technical changes

- Setup detects the required installed Windows x64 .NET Runtime before
  enabling the smaller runtime-required package and explains missing prerequisites.
  The standard package includes its runtime; WebView2 remains a separate prerequisite.
- Durable journal replacement and verified directory promotion retry short Windows
  sharing locks. Persistent locks still retain recovery data, and a changed source
  tree is rejected before a retry can promote it.
- Tracker projects are organized under Tracker, Setup, Updater, and Shared, with
  consistent namespaces and build-resource paths. Gameplay collection uses a
  dedicated SQLite layer with generated typed queries and reusable commands.
- Native `dotnet test` Quick/Full profiles replace the old PowerShell regression
  launchers. Routine PR checks cover important C# tests, bundled Ruby smoke tests,
  sprite contracts, and metadata; release preparation runs the full package gate.
  Runtime coverage now includes rival fusion, wardrobe transport/previews, and
  tracker UTF-8 text handling.
- The sprite-maintenance Python dependency is updated to Pillow 13.0.0.
- The README is shorter and links to a [full feature guide](../FEATURES.md).
  Installation/development guidance and the mechanics manual are refreshed, and
  the README explicitly discloses AI-generated code and artwork used by the mod.

## Installation and compatibility

Ironmon 0.10.0 is the stable release for **Pokémon Infinite Fusion 2: Hoenn 6.8.2**
on Windows x64. Keep game scripts and tracker from the same build together.
Existing runs retain versioned generation data; creating a new run uses the new
generation algorithms.

Download `Ironmon-Setup-win-x64.exe` for a new installation or to update a supported
existing installation. Setup now selects 0.10.0 by default. Players on an older
stable release can also update through **Settings > Check for updates** in the

This release freezes the exact accepted 0.10.0 test-build files without rebuilding
them. Players already using that final test build do not need to reinstall.
The temporary 0.8.16 upgrade-test bridge has been withdrawn after successful

For manual installation, choose one complete matching ZIP. The standard ZIP
includes .NET; the smaller runtime-required ZIP needs the Windows x64 .NET 10

download and metadata hashes.

    the slot order even when randomized types no longer form a type triangle.
  • After the first rival victory, the trainer policy determines whether the
    rival keeps its partner, swaps to the remaining offer, unfuses, or fuses the
    two normal offers. The resulting partner persists through the later story.
  • The lab sequence now handles those branches with Birch's assistance, native
    fusion animation, and movement around the player, furniture, and doorway.
    Rival fusion does not replace the player's party or register its Pokémon as
    the player's catches.
  • Rival fusion assignments and additional evolution work are prepared through
    the tracker. Large result imports are processed in smaller game updates to
    reduce long pauses after the opening battle.
  • A loss or draw in the Route 101 rescue or first rival battle always ends the
    attempt and queues a safe reset, including when automatic loss reset is off.
    The failed attempt is recorded and Archive opens without delaying reset for
    completed-run lookup calculations.
  • Earlier configuration-version-1 runs and seed data remain supported, retaining
    their original wild-controlled starter policy and rival plan.

Progression, rewards, and battle safeguards

  • Limited-party trainer battles now enter the current healthy Ironmon runner
    automatically, without asking the player to select a team. This includes
    Gym Leaders, regional adventurers, and move tutors. Type restrictions still
    apply, and multi-Pokémon quest hand-ins retain their normal selection rules.
  • The first Alpha endpoint is recorded as a win. Winning Wattson's normal
    Hoenn Gym battle completes the attempt, updates win statistics and achievement
    evidence, and saves the completed state after battle and event cleanup.
    Duplicate battle reports cannot award the win again.
  • A Pokémon Center recovery gift is available once per attempt. Its item is
    selected deterministically from the run's seed, so repeating the interaction
    does not reroll or repeatedly award the gift.
  • Direct scripted trainer rematches now obey the same challenge restriction as
    menu rematches, including rival and Tiana rematch paths. One-time story battles
    remain available.
  • Move-forgetting selection waits for Confirm/Cancel to be released before
    accepting a new input. Move-learning protection also prevents accelerated
    frames from carrying a held action straight into an unintended choice.

Tracker wardrobe and cosmetic rewards

  • Wardrobe editing now happens in a game-opened tracker dialog. Use the
    game's Change outfit command or bedroom wardrobe. Gameplay and the attempt
    timer pause while editing; Apply or Cancel returns to the game.
  • Fresh characters with an empty second accessory slot can open the wardrobe
    without the tracker disconnecting and reconnecting repeatedly.
  • Browse searchable outfits, hairstyles, and two accessory layers, with filters
    for all, owned, or unowned pieces. Locked pieces can be previewed before purchase.
  • Native previews cover the detailed portrait, front/back/side views, and bicycle.
    Skin tone, installed hair colors, and hair/clothes/accessory/bicycle dyes are
    editable, including precise hue values.
  • Named outfit profiles can be saved, applied, renamed, replaced, and deleted.
    Each save slot keeps its confirmed appearance through loading and resets.
  • Purchases are permanent even if an equipped preview is cancelled. Reconnection
    restores the current draft and ownership; physical Back can leave the wardrobe
    if the tracker disconnects.
  • Permanent unlock prices are five times their previous values. Existing
    point balances and owned pieces are retained without rescaling or extra charges.
    Colors and dye remain free, and the profile-wide additional free selection is
    retained until confirmed.
  • Each newly earned achievement grants 100 wardrobe points. Rewards are
    queued durably and credited once, including after a disconnect or lost
    acknowledgement. Achievement pop-ups do not need to be enabled. Achievements
    already earned before this reward system was introduced are not paid retroactively.

Persistent achievements and artwork

  • Fixed achievement tracking silently remaining inactive in clean Setup
    installations. Collector startup errors are now visible in protocol diagnostics.
  • A new Achievements page provides earned names, requirements, unlock dates,
    collection progress, search, and sorting. Progress and earned unlocks persist
    across attempts, resets, and save slots.
  • Locked names, conditions, and artwork stay concealed. Recorded evidence can
    contribute to later stages as their prerequisites become active.
  • Earned achievements have dedicated icons. Clicking supported earned icons
    opens their larger detail artwork. Artwork is shipped in protected embedded
    packs rather than loose image folders.
  • Compact in-game notifications show the earned icon and title, queue unlocks
    individually, and follow the game window's position and display size.
    They use a native Windows overlay without WPF, retaining sharp 50-, 75-, and
    100-pixel artwork, transparency, click-through behavior, and game-controlled timing.
  • Compatible achievement-definition and artwork updates retain earned identities
    and original unlock dates. Collection begins when the new recorder is used;
    importing a seed does not recreate older, unrecorded gameplay.

Gameplay collection and history maintenance

  • The tracker now records gameplay evidence in a persistent SQLite collection,
    covering Pokémon ownership and history, battle activity, resources, items,
    progression, and cosmetic events. Journaled delivery and duplicate protection
    support recovery across reconnects and interrupted sessions.
  • Settings > Maintenance reviews and exports unrelated history with the game
    closed. A closed game also permits maintenance after a connection-error state.
  • Review rehearses the real export, removal, and compaction on an owned temporary
    database copy. The displayed estimate is conservative net disk space freed,
    including the archive remaining on the same drive, rather than expanded JSON
    record size. The live database, WAL, and recipes remain unchanged during review.
  • Export creates a compressed, encrypted .irmhistory archive and verifies it
    before removing eligible source records. Protection is automatic: the player
    does not choose or receive a password.
  • Achievement evidence, earned unlocks, shared identities, live checkpoints, and
    Pokémon configuration chains remain in the active profile. Completion reports
    measured disk savings, including additional space used when an export grows.
  • Import restores an archive to its originating profile, merges it with newer
    evidence, and prevents duplicate counting. Keep exported files: future
    achievements may need detached history, and deleting the archive loses it.
  • Reconnecting the game discards a stale maintenance review and requires a fresh
    measurement before changing history.

Pokémon history, IVs, and archive inspection

  • Owned-Pokémon IV inspection adds recorded individual values to Pokémon
    lookup, including effective values and Hyper Training where that information
    is available. When several owned individuals share a species, their records
    can be inspected separately.
  • Archive Pokémon history retains the last Pokémon and earlier recorded
    starter, pivot, fusion, and evolution stages, with their highest recorded
    levels. Selecting a stage opens its archived species information.
  • Saved checkpoint boundaries trim discarded continuations after a reload,
    keeping the retained Pokémon timeline aligned with the saved attempt.
  • Archived sprites are reused offline. Missing history sprites can be requested
    from the connected game in bounded batches and cached for later viewing.
  • Losing opening-rival runs retain the context needed for later trainer-team
    inspection. Generating that preview is deferred until explicitly requested.

  • Trainer catalog generation now follows additional scripted story-battle paths
    and links multiple event identities to the correct trainer entry.
  • Rival, Wally, and other supported story teams can use their actual persistent
    story Pokémon when preparing trainer lookup, rather than treating every member
    as a fresh generic trainer randomization.
  • Trainer battle completion and item completion better follow their actual event
    identities, completion switches, and self-switches.
  • Encounter and obtainability calculations filter tables by the encounter methods
    the map can actually trigger, including land, cave, water, fishing, weather, and
    time variants. Unused encounter data no longer creates false available sources.
  • Early manual lookup preparation and authorized evolution inspection can prepare
    required fusion assignments before normal background lookup has started.
  • Additional cooperative checkpoints reduce long game-thread work during fusion
    closure, encounter expansion, and completed-run lookup preparation. Existing
    hidden-information restrictions remain in force.

  • An in-game battle item selector browses items and categories, remembers the
    selected item in each category between battles, and uses normal battle
    usability and targeting checks. Its controls are configurable in the tracker.
  • Five new battle bindings cover previous/next item, previous/next category, and
    use. Keyboard defaults use Ctrl+Shift with arrows and C; mapped controllers use
    both triggers with the D-pad and confirm button.
  • Settings > Speed edits independent overworld and battle Toggle cycles,
    using multipliers from 2× to 10×, custom order, repeated values, grouped stages,
    and links between contexts. Groups remember their selected member and define
    their first-entry speed. Normal speed remains first.
  • The speed editor includes Undo, Redo, and explicit Save changes. Hold mode
    retains the game's separate overworld/battle sliders. A new optional overworld
    indicator shows the active multiplier and cycle position; the Repel display
    uses the shared overlay styling.
  • Settings now have General, Controls, Features, Speed, and Maintenance pages.
    Features groups achievement pop-ups, Repel/speed indicators, item quick select,
    quick Run, Favorite Clause, BST enforcement, starter autoselection, automatic
    loss reset, and minimized startup.
  • Turning assistance off preserves its saved favorites, values, item selections,
    and bindings. Disabled quick-item/Run bindings remain visible but cannot be
    edited until their feature is enabled again.
  • A blank or zero starter BST ceiling means unlimited. Favorite Clause and BST
    enforcement can be switched independently of their saved settings. Saved-state
    feedback no longer shifts the Settings header as it appears.

Installation, documentation, and technical changes

  • Setup detects the required installed Windows x64 .NET Runtime before
    enabling the smaller runtime-required package and explains missing prerequisites.
    The standard package includes its runtime; WebView2 remains a separate prerequisite.
  • Durable journal replacement and verified directory promotion retry short Windows
    sharing locks. Persistent locks still retain recovery data, and a changed source
    tree is rejected before a retry can promote it.
  • Tracker projects are organized under Tracker, Setup, Updater, and Shared, with
    consistent namespaces and build-resource paths. Gameplay collection uses a
    dedicated SQLite layer with generated typed queries and reusable commands.
  • Native dotnet test Quick/Full profiles replace the old PowerShell regression
    launchers. Routine PR checks cover important C# tests, bundled Ruby smoke tests,
    sprite contracts, and metadata; release preparation runs the full package gate.
    Runtime coverage now includes rival fusion, wardrobe transport/previews, and
    tracker UTF-8 text handling.
  • The sprite-maintenance Python dependency is updated to Pillow 13.0.0.
  • The README is shorter and links to a full feature guide.
    Installation/development guidance and the mechanics manual are refreshed, and
    the README explicitly discloses AI-generated code and artwork used by the mod.

Installation and compatibility

Ironmon 0.10.0 is the stable release for Pokémon Infinite Fusion 2: Hoenn 6.8.2
on Windows x64. Keep game scripts and tracker from the same build together.
Existing runs retain versioned generation data; creating a new run uses the new
generation algorithms.

Download Ironmon-Setup-win-x64.exe for a new installation or to update a supported
existing installation. Setup now selects 0.10.0 by default. Players on an older
stable release can also update through Settings > Check for updates in the
tracker; enabling test releases is unnecessary.

This release freezes the exact accepted 0.10.0 test-build files without rebuilding
them. Players already using that final test build do not need to reinstall.
The temporary 0.8.16 upgrade-test bridge has been withdrawn after successful
upgrade testing; its signed build sequence remains reserved.

For manual installation, choose one complete matching ZIP. The standard ZIP

# Ironmon 0.8.12

Ironmon 0.8.12 fixes installation and update failures caused by downloaded game
data, player files, and mutable assets.

## Installer and updater fixes

- Recognize supported game installations after the game refreshes its downloaded
  settings, Pokedex data, sprite lists, credits, and download caches. These files
  no longer determine whether the installed game matches a supported release.
- Keep saves, imported generation profiles, custom sprites, and other player
  files outside program-file verification. Unrelated locked files and large
  player-data directories no longer block an otherwise valid update.
- Preserve player files during update preparation, installation, and rollback.
  Game upgrades retain existing assets, including player edits and removals,
  and install newly introduced default assets only where the path is vacant.
- Allow completed installations to be renamed or copied before the next update,
  and recover from damaged optional discovery caches or unrelated history.
- Check both supported game executable variants before replacing program files.

## Updating from an affected release

If an older tracker's updater rejects your installation, download and run
**Ironmon-Setup-v0.8.12-win-x64.exe**, then select your existing game folder.
The old updater still runs its original verification code; the new Setup is
needed to apply these fixes when that code prevents an in-app update.

Save your game before updating. Setup reviews program-file conflicts and retains
the installed tracker package flavor.

## Compatibility and downloads

scripts and tracker from the same release. The tracker remains required while
playing Ironmon. Existing runs retain their immutable generation profiles;

- **Settings > Game session > Start tracker minimized** replaces the optional
  game-start setting. Minimized startup keeps background services active.
- Loading an Ironmon save requires a compatible connected tracker. Existing
  Ironmon saves can still be continued with the matching tracker connected.
- A lost connection pauses Ironmon and its attempt timer. Reconnecting resumes
  the same attempt and battle. Ordinary non-Ironmon play remains available
  without the tracker.

## Create and continue runs

- Use the **Play header action** to create or continue an Ironmon run from the
  game's title screen or main menu. Title-screen actions skip the keypress,
  startup messages, and native menu. During gameplay, return to the title
  screen or main menu first.
- The new-run wizard has Save, Rules, and Review steps. Choose the game's actual
  **File A–H** slots and configure wild Pokémon, trainer Pokémon, and unfusion
  rules using reusable local profiles and help beside each setting.

  restores the previous save and starter checkpoint, with native backups kept.

  rules that expand across the full card below the right-aligned control.
- Shared seeds retain their separate action: start an Ironmon run, then import
  the seed into its active attempt.

  and the Ironmon reset hotkey together.
- Select the keyboard profile or a connected controller profile. Xbox,
  PlayStation, other mapped gamepads, and generic joystick buttons, directions,
  and axes are supported. Each controller keeps its own saved bindings.
- Set two independent bindings for each action, organized in category tabs.
  Restore the selected profile's defaults with its reset icon.
- Configure field interaction and the pause menu separately from menu
  confirmation, cancellation, and the guarded wild-battle Run shortcut.
- Assigning a conflicting binding removes it from the previous action and shows
  a warning. Actions used in separate contexts can still share a binding.

While the tracker is connected and the game is active, these profiles take
priority over the game's saved controls. Closing or disconnecting the tracker
restores native controls without rewriting the game's binding configuration.
The override also expires if the tracker stops responding.

- Enable **Settings > Startup > Start game with tracker** to open Infinite
  Fusion automatically when launching the tracker. The setting defaults to Off.
- An existing game from the same installation is reused. Closing the tracker
  leaves the game open, and closing the game does not automatically restart it.

  permanently visible.

# Ironmon 0.8.6

Ironmon 0.8.6 brings a redesigned tracker, revised trainer randomization and
boss parties, visible custom sprite validation, and live gym badge progress.
Release packages now pass automated validation against current upstream game
and sprite metadata before publication.

## Tracker and starter selection

- Redesign the tracker with a consistent dark interface across battle cards,
  settings, lookups, archives, research views, dialogs, and diagnostic tools.
- Preserve hidden enemy information, detailed move and defense information,
  nicknames, fusion identity, and temporary battle-stat changes.
- Add live eight-badge progress to player and enemy cards, center sprites in
  their shared panel, and retain both opponent selectors in double battles.
- Keep lookup content visible during paging and improve search and fusion
  candidate caching. Normal Pokemon inspection no longer starts global fusion
  preparation.
- Add independent Show all and Single row evolution-graph controls, configured
  neighborhood scope, route modes, and stable BST-group selection.
- Separate starter selection from sprite previews and preserve hidden/revealed
  states. Enforce the BST ceiling in both the game and tracker, including random
  selection; automatic selection uses only the random pick or eligible favorite.

## Trainer randomization and boss parties

- Select fully evolved randomized trainer species at effective level 30 or
  above without forcing story Pokemon to evolve at level 30.
- Preserve Wally's and the Hoenn main rival's policy-selected story Pokemon and
  their persistent evolution paths.
- Give the Hoenn main rival a normal starter under Normal Only, a planned
  normal-to-custom-fusion progression under Mixed, and a custom fusion from the
  start under Custom Fusions Only.
- Add three Pokemon, up to a party of six, to Wally, Gym Leaders, the Elite Four,
  Champion Steven, and the Team Aqua and Team Magma bosses. The Hoenn main rival
  is excluded from this party expansion.
- Keep live battles and World Lookup reconstruction aligned with the rules
  pinned by each generation profile, including archived version-1 profiles.

## Fusion preparation and sprites

- Detect isolated reverse-pair targets before exhaustive repair in the game
  and tracker. Impossible pairings fail with a diagnostic instead of exhausting
  repair work; successful pairing rules are unchanged.
- Require validated visible permitted custom sprite variants for new generation
  packages. Exclude blank or unavailable variants and pin the accepted variants
  into the generation profile.
- Preserve existing eligibility-version-1 profiles. Existing saved runs and
  encounters are not migrated or rerolled, and the proposed reverse-pair fallback
  remains disabled.
- Validate the committed sprite catalogue offline during PR checks; refreshing
  the full catalogue is a separate maintainer operation.

## Diagnostic access

- Add development controls gated by explicit capabilities and preserve existing
  permission boundaries in the redesigned diagnostics interface.
- Redesign the maintainer Access Generator, keep its window stable when changing
  presets, and improve signing-key selection and clipboard handling.
- Require removal of an active access token before importing another token.

## Release validation

- Run gameplay and tracker checks on every PR iteration against freshly resolved
  upstream game and online sprite metadata, using catalogs generated from the
  source under test.
- Build both Windows packages, checksums, provenance, and audit evidence for a
  release PR. Reuse matching verified candidates after merge, or rebuild and
  fully retest if source or upstream inputs have changed.
- Verify all release attachments before publishing the draft. New published
  releases protect their tags and attachments against modification.

scripts and tracker from the same 0.8.6 archive. The standard Windows x64 package

# Ironmon 0.8.5

Ironmon 0.8.5 improves wardrobe access, makes temporary transformed battle
state accurate in the tracker, aligns derived wild fusions with the encounters
that can actually coexist in the overworld, and refreshes the mechanics manual.

## Wardrobe

- Permanently unlock both male and female default outfits for every profile,
  including existing profiles loaded after the update.
- Add an explicit All items or Obtained only control to every normal wardrobe
  category browser while keeping locked pieces available for preview and
  purchase in the complete view.
- Preserve shared points and permanent ownership while keeping confirmed
  equipped appearance specific to each save slot.

## Imposter and Transform tracking

- Project the copied visible species, sprite, fusion identity, ability, types,
  base-stat total, non-HP battle stats, stat stages, and temporary 5-PP move set
  onto the live Player card after Imposter or Transform activates.
- Keep nickname, level, HP, status, gender, held item, nature, learnset,
  evolutions, and PP-restoring item targets attached to the original Pokemon.
- Continue showing only the original nature in its chip and suppress nature
  stat highlights while the displayed battle stats are copied.
- Keep persistent move and ability knowledge under the species that owns it,
  while recording the copied ability for the transformed species.
- Clear the temporary projection when the Pokemon leaves its transformed state.

## Derived wild fusions

- Restrict the 10% same-table and 5% cross-table standard fusion rolls to
  grass, cave, and surf-water encounters that can participate in visible
  overworld encounters.
- Exclude fishing and special encounters from both two-source rolls. Their
  authored rows may still map directly to a fusion when the selected wild
  policy permits fused results.
- Suppress Infinite Fusion's separate single-encounter random fusion roll
  during active Ironmon runs. With visible overworld encounters enabled,
  ordinary derived fusions now require two eligible visible participants;
  explicit forced story fusions remain supported.
- Apply the same eligibility boundary to tracker area totals, concealed derived
  rows, occurrence lookup, and obtainability material indexes.

## Mechanics reference

- Reorganize the mechanics manual with a descriptive contents index, clearer
  ownership overview, corrected wardrobe and attempt-ledger hierarchy, and
  improved navigation for screen and print layouts.
- Add captions and accessible headers to every table, convert attempt results
  and item weights into tables, and state the exact fusion-stat formula.
- Break dense tracker, area-lookup, evolution-graph, and obtainability sections
  into focused subsections while preserving their implemented behavior.
- Clarify the fishing boundary and the distinction between policy-mapped
  fusions and derived two-source encounters.

## Compatibility

Ironmon 0.8.5 targets Pokemon Infinite Fusion 2 version 6.8.2. Install the game
scripts and tracker from the same 0.8.5 archive. Both Windows x64 packages
contain the same features; the standard package includes .NET, while the
smaller runtime-required package needs the Windows x64 .NET 10 Runtime.
